waivers.reason: T-12's two: the prompt body renders Theme.typography.monoData 11sp where the design figure says 10.5px mono (no 10.5sp tabular-mono token exists and monoMeta is owned by the footer, so matching the figure would mean a new token for one composable); the Crops 'from frame #N' tag uses ink3 where the design's ink2 row implies ink2. waivers.item: Residual tech debt carried to Stage 6, not converted to CRs
waivers.reason: AF-4: crop cells are fitted to a constant CropCellWidth (84dp) but drawn in weight(1f), so the real cell is ~76dp at PanelMinWidth (clipping the right edge of the red outline) and ~149dp at PanelMaxWidth, and cropWindow's 'changes only on a different display' KDoc is therefore inaccurate. AF-6: PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION is dead code with a tautological test. Both are genuine and both are recorded for the Stage 6 tech review.

humanRemarks: Stage 5 found TWO real correctness defects that 251 green tests and 13 success reports had missed, both independently re-verified by the orchestrator before any fix was dispatched, and both now closed by targeted CRs with the re-audit green at 439 tests.

CR-1 (AF-1, AC-15): HierarchyOutline's `last` predicate used <= instead of <, marking any node FOLLOWED BY A SIBLING as last. Its guide stopped at the elbow while the sibling's line began at the next row's top, leaving a half-row gap before every non-final sibling — a ~400-node dump would have rendered as disconnected dashes. The deeper defect was the test: it asserted the buggy behaviour with a comment rationalising it, restating the implementation instead of HierarchyRow's documented contract. Fixed, comment rewritten to state the contract, and the tree extended so a final sibling WITH children now has a dedicated assertion (previously only root covered that case, accidentally).

CR-2 (AF-2, AC-80): a reachable state rendered hundreds of unbadged rows UNDER a 'no hierarchy' readout, because dumpHierarchyFor publishes the snapshot before reducing its verdict and the section's `when` tested rows.isNotEmpty() first. Triggered by the measured 9.76% uiautomator display-override mismatch — a real device condition, documented in HierarchySnapshotModel's own KDoc. Fixed by extracting the decision to core/payload/hierarchyOutlineDisplay() with status tested before row count, following the hasPayload precedent so branch ORDER is unit-testable. Six tests, with genuine red observed first.

ORCHESTRATOR ERROR, caught by the CR-2 implementer and verified: CR-2's brief offered 'stop publishing an unusable snapshot' as an equally acceptable fix. It is not. startMeasure reads snapshot.densityDpi, HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty carries densityDpi = 0, and PixelUnits degrades every figure to raw px below 1 — so that option would have fixed the payload tab while silently regressing the measure readout from dp to px in the same frame-size-mismatch condition. Option withdrawn from the record so nobody picks it later on diff-size grounds.

AF-3 was FIXED rather than deferred: StyleguideScreen.kt:744-745 passed a tag but no matched, a state the contract T-6 introduced says cannot exist, and that screen is reachable in the app via NavigationHost as the project's own component reference. Completing T-6's own call sites, not new scope.

ROOT CAUSE for Stage 7, raised by the CR-2 implementer and endorsed: THREE findings on this spec were the same shape — branch logic inside a @Composable that nothing in this repo can reach (AC-77's empty-state gate, AF-1's last predicate covered by a test that restated the implementation, AF-2's when-ordering whose preview evidence steered around the failing case). The pattern recurs until either a Compose UI-test harness exists or the convention is made explicit that no composable holds a branch condition it does not import from core/. The fix pattern is already proven three times in this spec (hasPayload, hierarchyOutlineDisplay) and is cheap.

Also noted: CR-2's fix makes dumpHierarchyFor HARMLESS, not correct — it still publishes a snapshot it has already judged unusable, and only the enum's KDoc stops the next consumer repeating the mistake. If a third consumer of frozenHierarchy appears, the right shape is a snapshot carrying its own usability verdict rather than two flows that can disagree.

Infra, not this spec: the Kotlin/Native release linker exhausts a 4 GiB daemon heap under ~4 parallel linkReleaseFramework* tasks. Fully characterized; --max-workers=1 passes. The real fix (kotlin.native.linkerThreads or a higher daemon -Xmx in gradle.properties) belongs in a standalone task, since TAC-6 forbade touching shared build files here.
